properties.description:
TORSHV

The National Weather Service in Shreveport has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Southeastern Union County in south central Arkansas...
Northeastern Union Parish in north central Louisiana...

* Until 515 PM CST.

* At 440 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located 5 miles southwest of Huttig, moving east at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Huttig, Felsenthal, Litroe and Cecil.
properties.instruction:
Move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built building
away from windows. If you are outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a
vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself
from flying debris.

Heavy rainfall is hiding this tornado. Do not wait to see or hear the
tornado. Take cover now!

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Topeka has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Kansas...

Big Blue River near Blue Rapids affecting Marshall County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Blue River near Blue Rapids.

* WHEN...From Thursday morning to Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 26.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding occurs from
Marysville to Tuttle Creek Lake.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CST Tuesday the stage was 17.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
Thursday morning to a crest of 26.8 feet Thursday evening. It
will then fall below flood stage early Friday morning.
- Flood stage is 26.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

This product along with additional weather and stream information is
available at www.weather.gov/top/.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 9:30AM EST until November 4 at 9:30AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...
Eastern Indian River County in east central Florida...
Northeastern Martin County in east central Florida...
St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 930 AM EST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. It will take several hours
for all the water from these storms to work through local drainage
systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 925 AM EST, flooding continues across the warned area and
emergency management has reported numerous road closures across
portions of southern Brevard County and the Treasure Coast.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Port Saint Lucie, Palm Bay, Melbourne, Walton, Fort Pierce,
Sebastian, Stuart, Vero Beach, Fellsmere, Indian River Shores,
Malabar, Indialantic, Vero Beach South, Gifford, Winter Beach,
Indrio, Wabasso, Sebastian Highlands, Fort Pierce Inlet and
Roseland.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:
Flooding along the Conejos River and San Antonio River continues.

* WHAT...Flooding along the Conejos River and San Antonio River,
caused by recent runoff from upstream rain and snowmelt, is
occurring.

* WHERE...Eastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
West Central Costilla County in south central Colorado...
South Central Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the Conejos River, from Mogote downstream
to Manassa, and the San Antonio River, near Ortiz downstream to
Manassa, is ongoing. Additional flooding of creeks, streams, and
other low-lying and flood-prone locations is possible. Numerous
roads remain closed due to flooding. Expect many areas of slow
moving or standing water through eastern Conejos County.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 347 PM MST, Upstream runoff from recent rain and snowmelt is
causing flooding into eastern Conejos County.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Manassa, Sanford, Antonito, Romeo, Alamosa East, Conejos and
Ortiz.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov

deaths occur in vehicles.

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Montezuma, CO; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:31PM MST until November 5 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the San Juan River caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...along the San Juan River from the Four Corners through
Mexican Hat, UT. This includes Bluff, Montezuma Creek and Aneth.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River levels continue to rise due to excess runoff from
Sunday's rainfall. Expect high water levels and the River exceeding
its banks, inundating low-lying areas along the San Juan River. A
prolonged period of high water is forecast, with a crest near 23.5
ft Thursday morning. It will take several hours for all the water
from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM MST, stream gauge reports upstream and impacts of
flooding have been reported along the San Juan River near
Farmington, NM. Expect flood waters to reach the Four Corners
Wednesday evening and the town of Bluff early Thursday morning.
Timing of crest is subject to change as more details become
available. Please continue to monitor the forecast and updated
warnings.
- At 11:30 AM MST Monday the stage was 20.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 22 feet late this evening with
a secondary crest near 23.5 feet expected near Bluff early
Thursday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Bluff, Montezuma Creek, and Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
